newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end with second day of gains.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end with second day of gains.

text.p: The Manila share index jumped 40.11 points, or 1.47 percent, to close at 2,776.53 points on Tuesday energised by follow-through buying on most blue chips and select secondliners, traders said.
"I think the Philippine market has a tendency to overshoot and given the Dow's rise as a backdrop, we see the market rallying," said Joey Salceda, director at SBC Warburg.
Turnover was a billion pesos less than Monday, but still a substantial 3.02 billion.
"It's already a cheap market compared with the region with PE level of 13 to 14 times from a high of 18 times," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities Phils.
Gainers outnumbered losers 81 to 57 with 63 issues unchanged. All sub-indices rose except for the mining sub-index.
But Sun Hung Kai Securities analyst Ramon Adviento said profit-taking may likely take place on Wednesday and trading volume could be thinner.

"I think this is part of the last hurrah rallies. I wouldn't be tempted with them. Weak property and banking sectors, low valuation and low earnings are an explosive combination. Caution is still the operative word," said SBC Warburg's Salceda.
Abacus Securities Corp research head Dennis Rayala said the buying momentum is technical in nature and would likely be shortlived.
"It does not really change the general sentiment. A lot of foreign funds are still underrating the Philippines," said Rayala.
